olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $p_1<p_2<\cdots$ be primes and $x_0\in(0,1)$. Define $x_k=\{p_k/x_{k-1}\}$ if $x_{k-1}\neq 0$ else $0$. Find all $x_0\in(0,1)$ for which the sequence eventually becomes 0.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1997

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $\triangle ABC$ have points $D,E,F$ on the perpendicular bisectors of $BC,CA,AB$. Show the lines through $A,B,C$ perpendicular to $EF,FD,DE$ are concurrent.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1997

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove that for any integer $n$, there is a unique polynomial $Q$ with coefficients in $\{0,1,\ldots,9\}$ such that $Q(-2)=Q(-5)=n$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1997

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A regular hexagon $P_6$ of area 1 is repeatedly clipped (cut off corner triangle $MBN$ where $M,N$ are midpoints of consecutive sides $AB,BC$). Prove the area of $P_n > 1/3$ for all $n\geq 6$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1997

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Nonneg­ative integer sequence $(a_n)$, $n=1,\ldots,1997$, satisfies $a_i+a_j\leq a_{i+j}\leq a_i+a_j+1$ for $i+j\leq 1997$. Show there exists real $x$ with $a_n=\lfloor nx\rfloor$ for $1\leq n\leq 1997$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1997
